newsitem.title: USA: Outback shares tumble on faltering sales.
newsitem.headline: Outback shares tumble on faltering sales.

text.p: Outback Steakhouse Inc shares fell sharply Friday in a selloff traders attributed to Outback telling analyst last night that its same-store sales fell 3.2 percent in December.
In morning Nasdaq trade Outback shares were off 1-1/4, or 4.5 percent, to 26-1/4 in unusually heavy volume.
Over 500,000 shares changed hands in the first hour of trading. Outback's average daily volume is about 340,000 shares.

In an interview with Reuters, an Outback spokeswoman confirmed the Tampa, Fla., restaurant chain had told analysts of the December sales falloff. She also said same-store sales for the fourth quarter fell 2.4 percent.
The slowdown was not surprising to analysts but was larger than expected, according to traders and the research note of at least one anaylst.

In that note, Alex. Brown analysts Steven Rockwell and David Trossman said they had been expecting a one percent decline in fourth quarter same-store sales. They called the December figure "disappointing."
Rockwell and Trossman trimmed Outback's earnings estimates but preserved their "strong buy" recommendation on the stock.
They said they now expect Outback to earn $0.38 per share in the fourth quarter, down from a previous forecast of $0.40.
The new earnings view for 1997 is $1.75 a share, down from $1.79, and for 1998 it is now $2.20, down from from $2.25.
The company spokeswoman said the December sales decline was due party to there being one less week in the period between Thanksgiving and Christmas this year compared with last year.
Outback earned $1.15 per share, or $53.6 million, in 1995 on revenue of $664 million, up from 1994's $0.88 per share, or $38.6 million, on revenue of $452 million.
The company, which operates 330 restaurants in 33 states, went public in June 1991 with an offering of 1.57 million shares at $15 each managed by Alex. Brown.
